subject: biology

items.q: A young shoot is lit from one side only and bends towards the light. Which explains this?
items.correct: Auxin gathers on the shaded side, which grows faster.
items.misconception: Auxin gathers on the lit side, which grows faster.
items.why: Students see the shoot bend towards the light and assume the hormone must move towards the light as well; textbook diagrams often shade one side without labelling where the auxin has gone. Unequal distribution of auxin places more auxin on the shaded side of the shoot. That side grows faster, so the shoot bends towards the light (phototropism).
items.random_wrong: Auxin gathers on the shaded side, which grows less.

items.q: A seedling is laid on its side in the dark. Which describes the response of its root?
items.correct: Auxin gathers on the lower side, which grows slower.
items.misconception: Auxin gathers on the lower side, which grows more quickly.
items.why: Auxin is first met as the hormone that makes shoots grow towards light, so students carry that single effect across to roots without checking it. Unequal distributions of auxin cause unequal growth rates in plant roots and shoots. In a root the side with more auxin grows less, so the root bends towards gravity (gravitropism).
items.random_wrong: Auxin collects on the upper side, which grows slower.

items.q: Which effect of a plant hormone is described correctly?
items.correct: Gibberellins are important in initiating seed germination.
items.misconception: Ethene is important in initiating germination of seeds.
items.why: The two hormones are met together in one short section and both are linked to seeds and fruit, so the names get swapped. Gibberellins are important in initiating seed germination. Ethene controls cell division and ripening of fruits.
items.random_wrong: Gibberellins are important in maintaining seed dormancy.

items.q: A farmer sprays a field of cereal plants with a weed killer containing auxins. What is the result?
items.correct: The weeds die and the cereal crop keeps growing.
items.misconception: The weeds and the cereal crop are both killed off.
items.why: Students think of weed killers as general poisons and do not expect a plant growth hormone to affect the weeds but not the crop. Auxins are used as weed killers in agriculture and horticulture. They upset the growth of the weeds, which die, while the crop plants are unaffected and grow on.
items.random_wrong: The weeds and the cereal crop both grow faster now.

items.q: Bananas are picked unripe and kept cool while they are shipped. Ethene is used on them when they arrive. Why?
items.correct: To start the fruit ripening at the end of storage.
items.misconception: To stop the fruit from ripening while it is stored.
items.why: Students know that fruit arrives in the shops unripe, so they assume the chemical that is added must be what is holding the ripening back. Ethene is used in the food industry to control ripening of fruit during storage and transport: it is used to bring on ripening, so ripening happens when the grower or seller wants it.
items.random_wrong: To keep the fruit firm until it is in the shops.

items.q: A grower treats a fruit crop with gibberellins. Which result would be expected?
items.correct: The fruits grow larger than untreated fruits.
items.misconception: The fruits ripen early, before reaching full size.
items.why: The two hormones are met together in one short section and both are linked to seeds and fruit, so the names get swapped. Gibberellins are important in initiating seed germination. Ethene controls cell division and ripening of fruits.
items.random_wrong: The seeds inside the fruits are kept in dormancy.

items.q: What is the effect of treating dormant seeds with gibberellins?
items.correct: The dormancy is ended, so the seeds are able to germinate.
items.misconception: Gibberellins are used to keep seeds dormant so that they can be stored for longer.
items.why: The phrase 'used to end seed dormancy' is read as 'used for seed dormancy', and students associate any treatment of seeds with keeping them in storage. Gibberellins can be used to end seed dormancy, promote flowering and increase fruit size.
items.note: no MCQ covers this misconception, so no third distractor was authored for it; none invented

specSource: AQA GCSE Biology (8461) specification; section 4.5.4 Plant Hormones (biology only)
